summary: Tenant sandbox permissions desync: devs unable to assume cross-account roles in staging projects
description:
Issue summary: Several developers reported they could no longer assume the cross-account role used for tenant sandbox access. Impact: Blocks feature testing and pre-release validation for two mid-size teams; prevents new workspace provisioning against staging projects. Scope: Affects users in staging AWS account and GCP preprod projects linked to the tenant-sandbox onboarding flow. First observed after a routine org policy rollout on 2026-02-17.

Primary symptoms: 'AccessDenied' on AWS AssumeRole, and 'Forbidden: Permission denied' in GCP when binding service accounts. Time window: 2026-02-17 23:00 UTC to present.

Desired outcome: Restore least-privilege cross-account/ cross-project role assumption for onboarding flows and document a safe rollback and permanent fix path.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Developer attempts to run 'make spawn-sandbox' which invokes the onboarding lambda to assume role arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/tenant-sandbox-deployer

2) AWS CLI error returned: 'User: arn:aws:sts::111111111111:assumed-role/infra-bot/session is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole on resource arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/tenant-sandbox-deployer',
3) In parallel, attempting to bind GCP workload identity to staging service account fails with: 'Permission 'resourcemanager.projects.setIamPolicy' denied.'
4) Attempting to run JIT grant path returned 403 when invoking the internal JIT service (https://console.internal/jit) with similar permission denied traces.
logs: 2026-02-18T02:12:04Z infra-bot sts: AssumeRole -> AccessDenied ARN: arn:aws:iam::222222222222:role/tenant-sandbox-deployer trace-id=tx-9c7f
2026-02-18T02:12:06Z onboarding-lambda ERROR Unable to create workspace: AccessDenied (sts:AssumeRole)
2026-02-18T02:18:22Z gcloud iam policies set -> Permission denied: resourcemanager.projects.setIamPolicy (project: rdl-staging-01) trace: prj-48d3
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: org-level IAM policy deployed 2026-02-17 contained a deny rule for broad 'setIamPolicy' and unconstrained sts:AssumeRole across sibling accounts. Confirmed via audit log: the policy introduced a DENY for principals with 'serviceAccount:*-infra-bot@redwood.iam.gserviceaccount.com' unless a tag 'allow-cross-project' present on target project. The staging projects did not have the tag.

SRE reproduced behavior by creating a minimal policy that matched the deny condition. Security confirmed the deny was intentional to close a previous privilege escalation path, but rollout omitted a list of exempt projects and the JIT-service principal.

Mitigation options evaluated:
- Rollback org policy (high blast radius)
- Add allow tag to staging projects (low risk)
- Update JIT/service principals to be explicitly allowed in the deny exception list (medium risk)

We chose quick, low-risk path: tag affected staging projects with 'allow-cross-project:onboarding' and add a short-lived exception binding for the JIT service principal. Also updated onboarding Lambda IAM role to use more specific principal and added explicit permissions to target role.

resolution:
Temporary fix: added 'allow-cross-project:onboarding' tag to affected staging projects and created a scoped exception for the internal JIT service principal. Permanent fix: updated onboarding-lambda to use a narrower principal and merged PR github.com/redwood/infra/pull/4812 to perform a preflight tag check; Security to create an explicit org-policy exception for the JIT principals in next policy release. Runbook updated: confluence.redwood.internal/ops/runbooks/iam-org-policy#onboarding-exceptions.

Follow-ups: INT-999001 (provision-scoped-ml-fleet-role) referenced for long-term role hardening; create a post-deploy verification job to validate onboarding flows when org policies change.
